key_insight: VLA-JEPA introduces a JEPA-style latent world model that learns leakage-free state predictions, focusing representations on action-relevant transitions rather than pixel-level changes.
problem_solved: Addresses the tendency of latent-action objectives to latch onto superficial pixel variation and nuisance motion, which causes appearance bias and information leakage in vision-language-action pretraining.
method: JEPA-style pretraining: learn to predict future latent states rather than raw pixels, forming a compact world model.
Leakage-free state prediction: use a target encoder design that prevents low-level appearance information from leaking into action representations.
Action-relevant alignment: optimize objectives that prioritize state transitions tied to agent actions and downstream control tasks, reducing sensitivity to nuisance motions.
impact: Makes VLA pretraining more robust and generalizable by producing action-focused latent representations, improving downstream policy transfer and reducing sensitivity to appearance changes in large-scale video data.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram comparing pixel-prediction vs. VLA-JEPA latent prediction (input video → encoder → leakage-free latent → predictor → target latent).
Before/after illustration showing susceptibility to appearance bias (confusing background motion) vs. correct action-relevant transitions.
Latent-space visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) showing tighter clustering by action/state rather than by appearance.
Ablation-style bar chart summarizing robustness gains (reduced leakage, improved transfer) across representative metrics.
paper_title: VLA-JEPA: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Model with Latent World Model
paper_authors: Jingwen Sun, Wenyao Zhang, Zekun Qi, Shaojie Ren, Zezhi Liu
